# jumpcloud_scim_attribute_mapping (Resource)

Manages one attribute mapping on the Provisioning (SCIM) tab of a JumpCloud application, e.g. mapping a group's custom attribute to a downstream user attribute. Built from captured browser requests against the console's IDMS API -- not documented anywhere else.

Only the `USER` resource type is supported. Rules the connector ships with (`default: true` in the API) can't be managed here. Changing any argument replaces the rule, because no update call has been captured. Mapping changes may need a resync from the console before they reach the downstream application; the console's resync endpoint is rate-limited and is not called by this resource.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Send a custom attribute of the user's groups to a downstream SCIM user attribute.
resource "jumpcloud_scim_attribute_mapping" "default_role" {
  idms_id     = "<the application's IDMS id>"
  destination = "urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:extension:2.0:User:defaultRole"
  source      = "jcGroups.attributes.defaultRole"
  source_type = "PATH"
}
```

## Finding the IDMS id

The provisioning (IDMS) id is not the application id, and no way to derive one from the other has been found. Open the application's Provisioning tab in the JumpCloud console with the browser's network tool open: the requests it makes go to `/api/v2/idms/<id>/...`.

## Import

A mapping is imported by `<idms_id>/<rule_id>`. Rule ids are in the response to `GET /api/v2/idms/<idms_id>/translation-rules`. Rules with `default: true` are the connector's own and can't be imported.

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `destination` (String) The downstream (SCIM) attribute to set, e.g. `urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:extension:2.0:User:defaultRole`.
- `idms_id` (String) The application's provisioning (IDMS) id: the id in the `/api/v2/idms/<id>/...` requests the console makes from the application's Provisioning tab. It is not the application id, and no way to derive it from the application id has been found.
- `source` (String) Where the value comes from. For `PATH`, a JumpCloud attribute path such as `email` or `jcGroups.attributes.myAttribute` (a custom attribute of the user's groups); for `CONSTANT`, the literal value; for `EXPR`, an expression in JumpCloud's mapping language.
- `source_type` (String) `PATH`, `CONSTANT` or `EXPR`.

### Optional

- `applied_on` (Set of String) When the rule fires: any of `CREATE` and `UPDATE`. Defaults to both, which is what the console sets.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.
- `rule_id` (String) The rule's own id, as used in the delete call.

## Notes

- A rule's `destination` must not already have a mapping: what the API does with two rules for one destination hasn't been observed, so creating one is refused. Remove the existing rule in the console first, or import it.
- Only the `USER` resource type has been exercised. A separate `USER_GROUP` rule type exists in the console and maps a group object, not a user attribute; it is not supported.
- This resource has been tested against a mock of the captured requests, not against the live API.
